# package socketcan

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/socketcan"
```

Package socketcan is the Linux SocketCAN transport: CAN\_RAW sockets with CAN FD, kernel filters, error frames, loopback control, kernel timestamps and drop accounting, and kernel ISO-TP sockets (CAN\_ISOTP).

It uses only the syscall package (no cgo). The socket is non-blocking and registered with the Go runtime's network poller, so blocked Send and Receive calls are ended by their context or by Close without extra goroutines.

Opening a socket never changes the interface: bit rates, CAN FD mode and the interface state are configured separately (package socketcan/link, or ip-link(8)).

On systems other than Linux the package compiles, and [Open](#func-open) and [DialISOTP](#func-dialisotp) return [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {

	// Receive and Send state, kept here so the poller callbacks (bound
	// once in Open) do not allocate per call.

	// struct sockaddr_can of the sender

	// CAN XL send buffer, allocated by Open with WithXL
	// what doWrite writes

	// ifindex → name, for "any"

}
```

Conn is a SocketCAN CAN\_RAW socket bound to one interface (or to all CAN interfaces, for the name "any"). It implements [canbus.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Transport), [canbus.Filterer](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Filterer), [canbus.Statser](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Statser), [canbus.DropCounter](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#DropCounter), [canbus.Namer](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Namer) and [canbus.Capabilitier](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Capabilitier). Opened with [WithXL](#func-withxl) it also sends and receives CAN XL frames ([Conn.SendXL](#func-conn-sendxl), [Conn.ReceiveXL](#func-conn-receivexl), [Conn.ReceiveAny](#func-conn-receiveany)).

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close closes the socket. Blocked Send and Receive calls return [canbus.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrClosed).

#### func (Conn) Drops

```go
func (c *Conn) Drops() (uint64, canbus.DropReason)
```

Drops returns the frames the kernel dropped because the socket's receive queue was full (SO\_RXQ\_OVFL). The kernel reports its counter with each received frame, so drops become visible with the first frame queued after them.

#### func (Conn) Name

```go
func (c *Conn) Name() string
```

Name returns the interface name ("any" for all interfaces).

#### func (Conn) Receive

```go
func (c *Conn) Receive(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Receive waits for the next frame. Error frames arrive only when the error mask selects them ([WithFilters](#func-withfilters)). Frames carry the kernel's receive timestamp, the interface name and the Echo mark. On a socket opened with [WithXL](#func-withxl), Receive skips CAN XL frames: use [Conn.ReceiveAny](#func-conn-receiveany) to get both kinds.

#### func (Conn) ReceiveAny

```go
func (c *Conn) ReceiveAny(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame, x *canbus.XLFrame) (xl bool, err error)
```

ReceiveAny waits for the next frame of any kind: a CAN or CAN FD frame is stored in f and reported with xl false, a CAN XL frame (on a socket opened with [WithXL](#func-withxl)) in x with xl true.

#### func (Conn) ReceiveXL

```go
func (c *Conn) ReceiveXL(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.XLFrame) error
```

ReceiveXL waits for the next CAN XL frame on a socket opened with [WithXL](#func-withxl), skipping CAN and CAN FD frames. f.Data's storage is reused.

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Send transmits a frame. A CAN FD frame needs a socket opened with [WithFD](#func-withfd). When the interface's transmit queue is full (ENOBUFS), Send retries until ctx ends.

#### func (Conn) SendXL

```go
func (c *Conn) SendXL(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.XLFrame) error
```

SendXL transmits a CAN XL frame on a socket opened with [WithXL](#func-withxl). When the interface's transmit queue is full (ENOBUFS), SendXL retries until ctx ends.

### type ISOTPConn

```go
type ISOTPConn struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ISOTPConn is a kernel ISO-TP socket (CAN\_ISOTP, Linux ≥ 5.10 or the can-isotp module). It implements [isotp.Endpoint](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/isotp#Endpoint).

#### func DialISOTP

```go
func DialISOTP(ifname string, cfg isotp.Config) (*ISOTPConn, error)
```

DialISOTP opens a kernel ISO-TP socket on the interface with the same configuration the userspace isotp.Conn takes. The kernel does not support Config.SendFlowWait, MaxWait other than its default (10), or N\_Bs/N\_Cr values other than its fixed 1 s; a Config asking for them is rejected with [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported). MaxMessageSize (default 4095) is at most 1025 KiB, the kernel's own bound; a larger one is rejected with [canbus.ErrInvalidOption](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrInvalidOption).

Close closes the socket.

```go
func (c *ISOTPConn) Receive(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)
```

#### func (ISOTPConn) Send

```go
func (c *ISOTPConn) Send(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) error
```

Send transmits one message and returns when the kernel has finished the transfer (or failed it: no flow control, overflow).

The kernel waits for the transfer inside sendmsg, interruptibly. Go's runtime signals its threads (SIGURG, for preemption); a signal would abort the transfer, and the syscall, restarted (SA\_RESTART), would send the whole message again. Send therefore runs the write on a locked OS thread with all signals blocked; they are delivered when it returns. The write cannot be cancelled once started: ctx is checked before only. The kernel's N\_Bs (1 s) bounds each wait for a flow control, not the transfer: a peer that keeps sending WAIT flow controls, or announces a long STmin, can extend it, and neither ctx nor Close ends it meanwhile.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures [Open](#func-open).

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD() Option
```

WithFD opens the socket for CAN FD (CAN\_RAW\_FD\_FRAMES). The interface must have the CAN FD MTU (72) or a CAN XL MTU (76..2060); otherwise Open fails with [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

#### func WithFilters

```go
func WithFilters(fs canbus.FilterSet) Option
```

WithFilters sets the kernel filters and error mask (CAN\_RAW\_FILTER, CAN\_RAW\_JOIN\_FILTERS, CAN\_RAW\_ERR\_FILTER). Without it the socket receives every data and remote frame and no error frame.

#### func WithReceiveBuffer

```go
func WithReceiveBuffer(n int) Option
```

WithReceiveBuffer sets SO\_RCVBUF in bytes. Larger buffers absorb longer bursts before frames are dropped.

#### func WithRecvOwn

```go
func WithRecvOwn() Option
```

WithRecvOwn delivers the socket's own transmissions back to it (CAN\_RAW\_RECV\_OWN\_MSGS), marked with [canbus.Frame.Echo](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Frame.Echo).

#### func WithSendBuffer

```go
func WithSendBuffer(n int) Option
```

WithSendBuffer sets SO\_SNDBUF in bytes.

#### func WithVCIDFilter

```go
func WithVCIDFilter(vcid, mask uint8) Option
```

WithVCIDFilter receives only CAN XL frames whose VCID matches vcid in the bits set in mask (CAN\_RAW\_XL\_VCID\_RX\_FILTER). It implies [WithXL](#func-withxl) and needs Linux ≥ 6.9.

#### func WithXL

```go
func WithXL() Option
```

WithXL opens the socket for CAN XL (CAN\_RAW\_XL\_FRAMES, Linux ≥ 6.2), which implies CAN FD: [Conn.SendXL](#func-conn-sendxl) sends CAN XL frames, [Conn.ReceiveXL](#func-conn-receivexl) and [Conn.ReceiveAny](#func-conn-receiveany) receive them. The interface must have a CAN XL MTU (76..2060, for example ip link set vcan0 mtu 2060); otherwise, or on a kernel without CAN XL, Open fails with [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

As cansend and candump do, the socket passes the VCID of sent frames through and receives frames of every VCID (CAN\_RAW\_XL\_VCID\_OPTS, Linux ≥ 6.9; older kernels ignore VCIDs). [WithVCIDFilter](#func-withvcidfilter) narrows reception.

#### func WithoutLoopback

```go
func WithoutLoopback() Option
```

WithoutLoopback disables local loopback (CAN\_RAW\_LOOPBACK 0): other sockets on this host do not see this socket's frames.

#### func WithoutTimestamps

```go
func WithoutTimestamps() Option
```

WithoutTimestamps does not request kernel receive timestamps (SO\_TIMESTAMPNS); frames then carry the time Receive returned.
